title: Emergency Medication
canonicalText:
[[PA.5204 | Emergency Medication | Applies to: PACE | Revised 08/01/2024]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy outlines the procedure for storing, maintaining, and administering emergency medications at
the CalOptima Health Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE) clinic.
II. POLICY
A. The CalOptima Health PACE clinic shall maintain a secured supply of emergency medication,
  approved by the CalOptima Health PACE Medical Director or designee, to address emergency
  medication needs for Participants.
III. PROCEDURE
A. The CalOptima Health PACE Clinic Manager, in consultation with the CalOptima Health PACE
  Medical Director, shall determine the drugs included in the emergency medication supply.
  1. The contents of the supply shall be listed on the outside of the container;
  2. The supply shall be checked at least quarterly by the pharmacist and
  3. Separate records of use shall be maintained for drugs administered from the supply. Such
    records shall include the name and dose of the drug administered, name of the participant, the
    date and time of administration and signature of the person administering the dose.
B. The CalOptima Health PACE Primary Care Provider (PCP) and RN shall not use more than three
  (3) doses in either sealed ampules or vials of any one (1) emergency drug.
  1. If an emergency medication is not available in parenteral form, a supply of the medication in
    inhalation or sublingual form may be maintained in the smallest sealed manufacturer’s package.
    No other oral legend (FDA Approved) drugs shall be stored.
C. CalOptima Health PACE shall store the emergency medication supply in the emergency supply cart
  which is locked.
<<page 2>>
D. Under the supervision of the CalOptima Health PACE PCP, during emergency or urgent conditions,
  medication from the emergency supply may be administered to a Participant by Physicians, Nurse
  Practitioners (NP), Physician’s Assistants (PA), Registered Nurses (RN), and Licensed Vocational
  Nurses (LVNs) according to each clinician’s scope of practice.
E. The CalOptima Health PACE PCP shall enter the order for use of the emergency medication in the
  Participant’s electronic medical record (EMR) according to the medication order procedures.
F. In the event of an emergency, the clinic nursing employees shall take the medication from the
  emergency drug supply under the direction of the CalOptima Health PACE PCP. The clinic nursing
  staff member shall record the date, name of the drug, number of doses dispensed, and their
  signature.
G. The PACE clinic nursing employees shall oversee the emergency medication supply and will keep
  the emergency supply locked. The emergency medical supply will be checked monthly and
  documented in the Emergency Kit Log.
H. Medications that are removed for Participant use will be replaced within seventy-two (72) hours
  after use and the supply re-locked by the CalOptima Health PACE licensed Nurse.
I. The CalOptima Health PACE clinic will maintain multiple doses of critical emergency medications
  on hand to ensure there are always emergency medications onsite.
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. CalOptima Health PACE Contract with the Department of Health Care Services for the PACE
  Program
B. CalOptima Health PACE Program Agreement
C. Title 22, California Code of Regulations (C.C.R.), §78317(i)
